name: Yemen

facts.religion: Sunni Islam about 60%, Zaidi Shia about 35%

system_note: The Houthis hold the north; a Saudi-backed government holds the rest.
snapshot: Saudi Arabia crushed the UAE-backed southern separatists in January, then the Houthis broke their truce with Riyadh in July and struck Saudi cities and shipping.
culture: Yemen was ancient Arabia Felix, home of the Queen of Sheba and the frankincense trade. The mud-brick tower houses of Shibam and Sanaa's old city are UNESCO-listed. Afternoon qat-chewing sessions are a social institution. Yemeni coffee from the port of Mocha gave its name to a drink. The jambiya dagger is worn by many men.
society: Yemen was the poorest Arab country before war began in 2014; since then the UN has called it one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with millions facing hunger and cholera. The Houthis control the north and most of the population. Their attacks on Red Sea shipping since 2023 drew US and Israeli strikes.
situation: Yemen has been at war since 2014, when the Iran-backed Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa. Saudi Arabia and the UAE intervened, and the anti-Houthi side splintered: the internationally recognised government on one side, a UAE-backed southern separatist movement, the Southern Transitional Council (STC), on the other. A UN truce from 2022 mostly held. Millions depend on food aid. In 2026 the map of Yemen was redrawn twice.

In December 2025 the STC grabbed the eastern provinces of Hadramawt and Mahra, on the Saudi border. Riyadh answered with airstrikes and Saudi-backed troops; within days the STC collapsed, its leader Aidarous al-Zubaidi fled to the UAE and was charged with treason, government forces took Aden, and the Emiratis withdrew (Sanaa Center). Saudi Arabia now has unrivalled sway over the anti-Houthi camp for the first time, and a new government was formed on 6 February. Southern separatism did not vanish: in April STC supporters reopened party offices in Aden and tore down Saudi flags (South24). The Houthis held back at first. Then in July, as the Iran war dragged on, their truce with Riyadh collapsed: they declared a blockade of Saudi shipping, hit the Aramco refinery in Jizan and in September struck four Saudi cities, wounding 73. In the north, the Houthis rule some 20 million people under US terrorism designation, with fuel and food scarce.
power: A divided country. The Presidential Leadership Council, created in 2022 with Saudi backing, is the recognised government, based in Aden. The Houthis govern Sanaa and most of the populous northwest through their own administration.
holders: Rashad al-Alimi, chairman of the Presidential Leadership Council; Houthi leader Abdul-Malik al-Houthi.
